blueprint_concepts: Locus problems: midpoints of chords, feet of perpendiculars

concept_use.Locus based questions: Both K1 and K2 are found as loci (circles) of a moving point defined by a right-angle condition.
concept_use.Locus problems: midpoints of chords, fee: K1 is the locus of midpoints of chords through P (circle on OP) and K2 the locus of feet of perpendiculars from Q (circle on PQ).

english: Let $\Gamma$ be the circle $x^2+y^2=16900$, and let $P(100,75)$ and $Q(40,-30)$. Let $K_1$ be the locus of the midpoints of the chords of $\Gamma$ that pass through $P$, and let $K_2$ be the locus of the feet of the perpendiculars drawn from $Q$ to the lines passing through $P$. Then the length of the common chord of $K_1$ and $K_2$ is ______.
hindi: माना $\Gamma$ वृत्त $x^2+y^2=16900$ है, तथा $P(100,75)$ और $Q(40,-30)$ हैं। माना $K_1$, $\Gamma$ की उन जीवाओं के मध्य-बिन्दुओं का बिन्दुपथ है जो $P$ से होकर जाती हैं, तथा $K_2$, $Q$ से $P$ से होकर जाने वाली रेखाओं पर डाले गए लम्बों के पादों का बिन्दुपथ है। तब $K_1$ तथा $K_2$ की उभयनिष्ठ जीवा की लम्बाई ______ है।
solution: $P$ is inside $\Gamma$ ($100^2+75^2=15625<16900$). Midpoint $M$ of a chord through $P$: $OM\perp PM$, so $K_1$ is the circle on $OP$: $x^2+y^2-100x-75y=0$
Foot $F$ from $Q$: $QF\perp PF$, so $K_2$ is the circle on $PQ$: $(x-100)(x-40)+(y-75)(y+30)=0$, i.e. $x^2+y^2-140x-45y+1750=0$
Centre of $K_1$ $(50,37.5)$, radius $62.5$; distance to the chord $=\dfrac{|200-112.5-175|}{5}=17.5$
Half chord $=\sqrt{62.5^2-17.5^2}=60$, so the length is $120$
solution_full: $100^2+75^2=15625<16900$, so $P$ lies inside $\Gamma$ and every line through $P$ cuts a chord.

If $M$ is the midpoint of a chord through $P$, then $OM\perp$ chord, so $\angle OMP=90^\circ$ and $M$ lies on the circle with diameter $OP$. Conversely every point of that circle (inside $\Gamma$, which holds since the whole circle lies inside $\Gamma$) is such a midpoint. $K_1:x(x-100)+y(y-75)=0$, i.e. $x^2+y^2-100x-75y=0$.

If $F$ is the foot of the perpendicular from $Q$ to a line through $P$, then $\angle QFP=90^\circ$, so $F$ lies on the circle with diameter $PQ$. $K_2:(x-100)(x-40)+(y-75)(y+30)=0$, i.e. $x^2+y^2-140x-45y+4000-2250=0$, so $x^2+y^2-140x-45y+1750=0$.
$K_1$ has centre $(50,37.5)$ and radius $\frac12OP=62.5$. Its distance from the chord is $\dfrac{|4(50)-3(37.5)-175|}{5}=\dfrac{87.5}{5}=17.5$.

Check: the two circles meet at $P(100,75)$ and at $(28,-21)$, the foot of the perpendicular from $P$ on $OQ$ (both right angles at that point make $O$, it and $Q$ collinear); the distance between them is $\sqrt{72^2+96^2}=120$.
originality_note: New: two different loci through the same point P (midpoints of chords through P, feet of perpendiculars from Q to lines through P) are both circles, and their second common point is the foot of the perpendicular from P to OQ (way 4: hidden collinearity). Closest known: 'locus of midpoints of chords through a point is a circle'. Different because: the question compares two loci and their common chord, which the hidden right angles make clean.
stem_review: Read as a student: every point, line, curve and symbol is introduced before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed independently with sympy/mpmath (and a numerical brute-force check), is unique and equals the Answer Plan. Stated the circle Gamma so that P is inside it and K1 is the full circle on OP. Changed: No change.
key_step: Recognising both loci as circles on OP and PQ as diameters, then the common chord by subtraction.
justification: Two standard locus results and a routine common-chord computation; numerical but every step is practised. Comparable to the routine circle chains rated 2 (2026-P1-Q2, L2).
